gaps.sentence: The film was ___ good, but not brilliant.
gaps.hint: an adverb of degree is needed before 'good'
gaps.explanation: 'Quite' means fairly or rather; 'quiet' is an adjective meaning without noise.

gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.

gaps.sentence: The committee acted on legal ___ before revising the clause.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the noun; 'advise' is the verb.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: The book gives a detailed ___ account of the period.
gaps.hint: connected with the study of the past
gaps.explanation: 'Historical' means relating to history or the past; 'historic' means important in history.

gaps.sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.
